definition: Spatial embedding is one of feature learning techniques used in spatial analysis where points, lines, polygons or other spatial data types.
details: representing geographic locations are mapped to vectors of real numbers. Conceptually it involves a mathematical embedding from a space with many dimensions per geographic object to a continuous vector space with a much lower dimension. Such embedding methods allow complex spatial data to be used in neural networks and have been shown to improve performance in spatial analysis tasks

explainer.lead: Spatial embedding maps spatial data types—points, lines, polygons and other geographic objects—to vectors of real numbers. It matters because it turns complex spatial data into a low-dimensional continuous form usable in neural networks, improving performance on spatial analysis tasks.

tiers.eli5: It is like giving every place on a map a short list of numbers so a computer can compare locations mathematically.
tiers.practitioner: Analysts embed geographic objects into continuous vectors so neural networks can consume them in spatial analysis. A pitfall is that compressing many dimensions per object into far fewer can lose detail.
tiers.paperLevel: A feature-learning technique in spatial analysis performing a mathematical embedding from a space with many dimensions per geographic object to a continuous vector space of much lower dimension.

explainer.example: A polygon representing a city district is encoded as a low-dimensional vector and fed into a neural network that predicts local demand.
